title: Sell Mineral Rights in Irwin, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Irwin, PA
metaDescription: Irwin, PA sits atop layered coal, coke, and Marcellus history. Understand what your mineral interest covers before you get an offer.
heroLead: Irwin was built on coal and coke money, and a hundred years later the gas underneath the same ground is what's bringing landmen back to Westmoreland County.
intro: Irwin's history is coal history — the Westmoreland Coal Company ran mines through here in the late 1800s, and plenty of the mineral deeds you'll find recorded in Greensburg reserved coal specifically, sometimes without ever mentioning oil and gas at all. That distinction matters more than most people realize, because owning coal rights under an Irwin tract doesn't automatically mean you own the gas rights, and the reverse is just as often true.

sections.heading: Coal Deeds vs. Gas Deeds — Not the Same Thing
paragraphs: A lot of confusion around Irwin comes from deeds written in an era when nobody thought oil and gas mattered much. Coal companies bought coal, full stop, and left oil, gas, and other minerals with the surface owner or a different chain of title entirely. If your family's deed only mentions coal, you may still hold gas rights nobody has ever leased — worth checking before you assume you have nothing to sell.

sections.heading: Why the Marcellus Changed the Math
paragraphs: For decades the old coal severances around Irwin sat idle as far as gas was concerned. Horizontal Marcellus drilling changed that because operators can now reach thousands of feet of lateral wellbore from a single pad on the edge of a developed borough like Irwin, pulling gas from under residential streets and old farmland alike without disturbing the surface. That's what put Irwin-area gas rights back in play after sitting dormant for generations.

sections.heading: What We Check Before Making an Offer
paragraphs: On every Irwin parcel we look at, we confirm whether the reservation is coal, oil and gas, or both, whether it's been leased before, and what unit — if any — has been filed against it. Depending on what that record shows, and what nearby royalty checks are running, we put together a range instead of pulling a number out of thin air.

faqs.question: My family only ever talked about the coal rights — do we have gas too?
faqs.answer: Sometimes yes. Old severance language varies a lot in this part of Westmoreland, so we pull the actual deed language rather than guessing from family memory.

faqs.question: Is a residential lot in Irwin borough worth checking?
faqs.answer: If minerals were severed before the lot was subdivided, yes — plenty of streets in Irwin sit above old undivided interests.

faqs.question: What does 'unleased' mean for value?
faqs.answer: Unleased minerals typically carry more upside than a leased tract that's already committed to fixed royalty terms, but it varies with how active nearby drilling is.
